name: Pune International Airport
before:
Pune's airport, about 11 km north east of the historic centre, serving Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad. It is ninth busiest in India and handled over 10.4 million passengers in the 2024-25 financial year.

The quality is better than the size suggests. In 2025 Airports Council International ranked it first among Indian airports for service quality in its size band, scoring 4.96 out of 5.

The constraint is that it is not really a civil airport. It is a civil enclave on the western side of Lohagaon Air Force Station, and air traffic control is run by the Indian Air Force. That causes recurring friction over flight schedules and night landings. Night landings for civil flights are currently allowed, but the arrangement is described as a working compromise rather than a settled one, so late arrivals carry more schedule risk here than elsewhere.

The single runway is 2,540 metres. Pune Metro reaches Ramwadi station about 3 km from the terminal, with feeder buses connecting the two.

A renaming to Jagadguru Sant Tukaram Maharaj Airport has been approved by the state government.
after:
Pune's airport, about 11 km north east of the historic centre. It is ninth busiest in India and handled just over 11 million passengers in the 2025-26 financial year.

The airport is a civil enclave run by the Airports Authority of India, while the Indian Air Force runs air traffic control and approves flight slots.

Pune Metro does not reach the airport, but PMPML city buses serve it.

Sources disagree: Wikipedia gives 2,540 m in its text and 2,539 m in its infobox and calls the old second runway a taxiway, while OurAirports lists two runways, 10/28 at 3,048 m and 14/32 at 1,796 m. India's eAIP could not be opened to settle it (its menu page answered 404).
